algorithm: Breadth-first search the reachable canonical binary strings, pruning successors longer than the target.
correctness_argument: After the first operation every state ends in one. Subsequent zero-appends only reverse it, and one-appends add one at an end after reversal; lengths can no longer shrink. The original state is always expanded even if it is longer, allowing its trailing zeros to be removed. Thus pruning successors above the target length is safe and the finite search is exhaustive.
problem_understanding: Represent both positive integers as canonical binary strings.

steps.claim: Implementation follows these obligations: Represent both positive integers as canonical binary strings. Generate append-zero and append-one followed by reverse and leading-zero removal. Every generated state is odd, so future transitions cannot shorten it. Prune generated states longer than the target and deduplicate them. Test the initial state as well, allowing zero operations.
